headline: Nepali Congress sets October 5 nominations as Deuba urges boycott
dek: Deuba's camp plans its own December convention, and the Supreme Court agreed in August to review its April ruling backing Thapa, Kathmandu Post reported.
body_markdown:
Nepali Congress's Central Election Committee, which organises the party's internal vote, has set Monday, October 5, Ashoj 19 on the Nepali calendar, as the day to register nominations for the Central Working Committee, the panel that leads the party between conventions. Registration runs from 2pm to 6pm that day, DC Nepal reported. Party Vice President Bishwa Prakash Sharma told OnlineKhabar there will be no panel system this year. Delegates will vote for individual candidates of their choice, not a faction slate, he said at the convention venue in Khulamanch. About 7,500 delegates are expected to take part, Setopati reported.

That is the story most outlets are telling today. It is only half the story. Nepali Congress, one of Nepal's oldest political parties, is not holding one convention. It is holding two, two months apart.

Former Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba, who led Nepali Congress before the January special convention and now leads a rival faction, has urged party leaders and members not to attend the October convention at all. He called it the product of an "illegal special convention" and warned that going ahead without the majority of leaders would weaken the party, Desh Sanchar reported. Deuba's own camp has scheduled a separate general convention for Mangsir 21 to 23, which falls in roughly December 7 to 9, Desh Sanchar reported.

The split goes back to a special convention in January, where Gagan Thapa, now Nepali Congress president, won control of the party's leadership. Deuba's side challenged that vote in court. The Supreme Court ruled in Thapa's favour in April, Kathmandu Post reported. Deuba and Purna Bahadur Khadka then filed review petitions. In August the court agreed to review its own ruling, the paper reported on August 7. Thapa stays president until a fresh ruling, it reported. Kathmandu Post reported in August that Deuba's supporters wanted the entire convention process postponed until that review was decided.

The review has not stopped Thapa's side. The establishment faction scheduled its 15th General Convention for October 2 to 5, with ward level conventions scheduled from September 19, Kathmandu Post reported. Deuba's own ranks are thinning at the same time. More than 30 leaders who had backed Deuba are now moving toward Thapa's committee, after the party agreed to accommodate members earlier elected under Deuba's leadership, Kathmandu Post reported. Purna Bahadur Khadka, Nepali Congress's former acting president, led Deuba's faction for several months. He has since moved toward Thapa's committee, Kathmandu Post reported.

## What the coverage missed

None of today's reports on the October 5 nomination date say whether the roughly 7,500 delegates include Deuba's camp at all. Nepali Congress has not published a breakdown by faction. Deuba's side is not filing nominations on October 5. It is building toward its own convention two months later instead.

The nominations are also going ahead while the Supreme Court reviews the ruling behind them. The court agreed in August to review its April verdict that backed Thapa's committee, Kathmandu Post reported on August 7. DC Nepal, Ekantipur, Setopati and OnlineKhabar did not raise this in reporting the nomination date.

## What we still do not know

- Whether Deuba's side will ask the Supreme Court to block or unwind decisions taken at the October convention before its own December gathering. The court's registrar and Deuba's lawyers could answer this.
- How many of the party's roughly 7,500 delegates each faction now counts as its own. Nepali Congress's Central Election Committee has not published a breakdown.

take: Four outlets reported today's nomination date, and all four missed that Nepali Congress is now split between two rival camps holding two separate conventions. Sher Bahadur Deuba, the former prime minister, has told members to skip the October convention entirely, calling it the product of an "illegal special convention." His camp is building its own convention for December. The Supreme Court agreed in August to review its April ruling that backed Gagan Thapa, now party president, Kathmandu Post reported. Readers deserve to know which camp they are actually reading about.

Nepali Congress set October 5 for nominations to its top committee. No panels this year, Vice President Bishwa Prakash Sharma said. About 7,500 delegates are expected, Setopati reported.

Former prime minister Sher Bahadur Deuba wants members to boycott the convention. He calls it the product of an "illegal special convention". His camp has set its own convention for Mangsir 21 to 23, roughly December 7 to 9, Desh Sanchar reported.

The Supreme Court agreed in August to review its April ruling backing Gagan Thapa, the party president, Kathmandu Post reported. More than 30 leaders who backed Deuba are moving toward Thapa's committee, the paper reported.

nepali.headline: कांग्रेसको मनोनयन ५ अक्टोबरमा, देउवाको बहिष्कार आह्वान
nepali.dek: देउवा पक्षले डिसेम्बरमा आफ्नै महाधिवेशन तय गरेको छ भने सर्वोच्च अदालतले थापाको पक्षमा गरेको अप्रिलको फैसला अगस्टमा पुनरावलोकन गर्ने निर्णय गरेको काठमाडौं पोस्टले उल्लेख गरेको छ।
nepali.take: चार सञ्चारमाध्यमले आजको मनोनयन मितिको खबर दिए, तर चारैले एउटा कुरा छुटाए। नेपाली कांग्रेस अहिले दुई प्रतिस्पर्धी समूहमा बाँडिएको छ, र दुईले छुट्टाछुट्टै महाधिवेशन गरिरहेका छन्। पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाले सदस्यलाई अक्टोबरको महाधिवेशन पूरै बहिष्कार गर्न भनेका छन्, र यसलाई "अवैध विशेष महाधिवेशन"को उपज भनेका छन्। उनको पक्षले डिसेम्बरमा आफ्नै महाधिवेशन तय गरेको छ। सर्वोच्च अदालतले अप्रिलमा पार्टी सभापति गगन थापाको पक्षमा गरेको फैसला अगस्टमा पुनरावलोकन गर्ने सहमति जनाएको काठमाडौं पोस्टले उल्लेख गरेको छ। तपाईंले कुन पक्षको खबर पढिरहनुभएको छ, त्यो थाहा पाउनु तपाईंको अधिकार हो।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । नेपाली कांग्रेसको भित्री चुनाव गराउने केन्द्रीय निर्वाचन समितिले केन्द्रीय कार्य समितिमा मनोनयन दर्ता गर्ने दिन सोमबार (५ अक्टोबर) अर्थात् असोज १९ तोकेको डीसी नेपालले जनाएको छ। केन्द्रीय कार्य समितिले दुई महाधिवेशनबीच पार्टी चलाउँछ। डीसी नेपालका अनुसार दर्ता दिउँसो २ बजेदेखि साँझ ६ बजेसम्म हुनेछ।

खुलामञ्चको महाधिवेशनस्थलमा कांग्रेस उपाध्यक्ष विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले अनलाइनखबरलाई यस पटक प्यानल प्रणाली नहुने बताए। प्रतिनिधिले गुटको सूचीलाई होइन, आफूले रोजेका उम्मेदवारलाई भोट दिने उनले भनेका छन्। महाधिवेशनमा करिब ७,५०० प्रतिनिधि सहभागी हुने सेतोपाटीले जनाएको छ।

यो आजको धेरैजसो सञ्चारमाध्यमले दिएको खबर हो। तर यो कथाको आधा मात्र हो। नेपालका पुराना दलहरूमध्ये एक नेपाली कांग्रेसमा अहिले एउटा होइन, दुई महिनाको फरकमा दुईवटा महाधिवेशन हुँदैछन्।

पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाले नेता र सदस्यलाई अक्टोबरको महाधिवेशनमा पटक्कै सहभागी नहुन आह्वान गरेको देश सञ्चारले जनाएको छ। जनवरीको विशेष महाधिवेशनअघि उनले नेपाली कांग्रेसको नेतृत्व गरेका थिए। अहिले उनी प्रतिस्पर्धी समूहको नेतृत्व गरिरहेका छन्। देश सञ्चारका अनुसार उनले यसलाई "अवैध विशेष महाधिवेशन"को उपज भनेका छन्। बहुमत नेताबिना अघि बढ्दा पार्टी कमजोर हुने चेतावनी पनि उनले दिएको देश सञ्चारले लेखेको छ। देश सञ्चारका अनुसार देउवाको आफ्नै समूहले मंसिर २१ देखि २३ सम्म, अर्थात् करिब ७ देखि ९ डिसेम्बरसम्म छुट्टै साधारण महाधिवेशन तय गरेको छ।

यो विभाजन जनवरीको विशेष महाधिवेशनबाट सुरु भएको हो। त्यहाँ हालका पार्टी सभापति गगन थापाले नेतृत्वको नियन्त्रण पाएका थिए। देउवा पक्षले त्यो मतलाई अदालतमा चुनौती दिएको थियो। सर्वोच्च अदालतले अप्रिलमा थापाको पक्षमा फैसला गरेको काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। त्यसपछि देउवा र पूर्णबहादुर खड्काले पुनरावलोकन निवेदन दिए। अदालतले अगस्टमा आफ्नै फैसला पुनरावलोकन गर्ने सहमति जनाएको काठमाडौं पोस्टले ७ अगस्टमा जनाएको छ। नयाँ फैसला नआउँदासम्म थापा नै सभापति रहने सोही पत्रिकाले जनाएको छ। काठमाडौं पोस्टले अगस्टमा जनाएअनुसार देउवा समर्थकहरू पुनरावलोकनको टुंगो नलागेसम्म सम्पूर्ण महाधिवेशन प्रक्रिया स्थगित होस् भन्ने चाहन्थे।

पुनरावलोकनले थापा पक्षलाई रोकेको छैन। संस्थापन पक्षले १५औं साधारण महाधिवेशन २ देखि ५ अक्टोबरसम्म तय गरेको काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। वडास्तरीय महाधिवेशन १९ सेप्टेम्बरदेखि तय गरिएको पनि सोही पत्रिकाले उल्लेख गरेको छ। यसबीच देउवा पक्षमा नेताहरू घट्दै गएका छन्। देउवाको नेतृत्वमा पहिले निर्वाचित सदस्यलाई समायोजन गर्न पार्टी सहमत भएपछि देउवालाई साथ दिएका ३० भन्दा बढी नेता अहिले थापाको समितितर्फ ढल्किँदै गएको काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ। नेपाली कांग्रेसका पूर्व कार्यवाहक सभापति पूर्णबहादुर खड्काले केही महिना देउवा पक्षको नेतृत्व गरेका थिए। त्यसयता उनी पनि थापाको समितितर्फ ढल्केको काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

५ अक्टोबरको मनोनयन मितिबारे आजको कुनै पनि रिपोर्टले करिब ७,५०० प्रतिनिधिमा देउवा पक्ष समावेश छ कि छैन भन्ने उल्लेख गरेको छैन। नेपाली कांग्रेसले गुटगत विवरण सार्वजनिक गरेको छैन। देउवा पक्षले ५ अक्टोबरमा मनोनयन दर्ता गर्दैन। बरु उनीहरू दुई महिनापछि आफ्नै महाधिवेशनतिर लागिरहेका छन्।

मनोनयन प्रक्रिया अघि बढिरहेकै बेला सर्वोच्च अदालतले यसको आधार बनेको फैसला पुनरावलोकन गरिरहेको छ। अदालतले थापाको समितिलाई समर्थन गर्ने अप्रिलको फैसला अगस्टमा पुनरावलोकन गर्ने सहमति जनाएको काठमाडौं पोस्टले ७ अगस्टमा जनाएको छ। डीसी नेपाल, इकान्तिपुर, सेतोपाटी र अनलाइनखबरले मनोनयन मितिको खबर दिंदा यो विषय उठाएनन्।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

- देउवा पक्षले आफ्नो डिसेम्बरको महाधिवेशनअघि अक्टोबरको महाधिवेशनमा लिइने निर्णयलाई रोक्न वा उल्टाउन सर्वोच्च अदालतमा जाने हो वा होइन। यसको जवाफ अदालतको रजिस्ट्रार र देउवाका कानुन व्यवसायीले दिन सक्छन्।
- पार्टीका करिब ७,५०० प्रतिनिधिमध्ये कुन समूहले अहिले कति जनालाई आफ्नो मान्छ। नेपाली कांग्रेसको केन्द्रीय निर्वाचन समितिले यसको विवरण सार्वजनिक गरेको छैन।

fact_problems: The record says Deuba's supporters wanted the process postponed. रोक्न means stop, which is a different and stronger demand than postponing, and माग गरेको is firmer than 'wanted'.
The record says these leaders are 'moving toward' Thapa's committee. समितिमा गइरहेको reads as joining the committee, which is stronger than the record.

language_fixes.passage: नेपाली कांग्रेस ५ अक्टोबरमा मनोनयन गर्दै छ, तर पार्टी दुई पक्षमा बाँडिएको छ।
language_fixes.problem: मनोनयन गर्दै छ reads as the party appointing people, but the news is that candidates register their nominations. The line also repeats the card's first line, '५ अक्टोबरमा मनोनयन'.
language_fixes.fix: नेपाली कांग्रेस अहिले दुई पक्षमा बाँडिएको छ, र दुई महिनाको फरकमा दुईवटा महाधिवेशन हुँदै छन्।

language_fixes.passage: सर्वोच्च अदालतले अप्रिलमा पार्टी सभापति गगन थापाको पक्षमा गरेको फैसला अगस्टमा पुनरावलोकन गर्ने सहमति जनाएको काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ।
language_fixes.problem: The same verb, जनाएको, appears twice in one sentence, so the line reads clumsily.
language_fixes.fix: सर्वोच्च अदालतले अप्रिलमा पार्टी सभापति गगन थापाको पक्षमा गरेको फैसला अगस्टमा पुनरावलोकन गर्ने सहमति जनाएको काठमाडौं पोस्टले उल्लेख गरेको छ।

language_fixes.fix: बहुमत नेताबिना अघि बढ्दा पार्टी कमजोर हुने चेतावनी पनि उनले दिएको देश सञ्चारले लेखेको छ। देश सञ्चारका अनुसार देउवाको आफ्नै समूहले मंसिर २१ देखि २३ सम्म, अर्थात् करिब ७ देखि ९ डिसेम्बरसम्म छुट्टै साधारण महाधिवेशन तय गरेको छ।

language_fixes.fix: प्रतिनिधिले गुटको सूचीलाई होइन, आफूले रोजेका उम्मेदवारलाई भोट दिने उनले भनेका छन्।

language_fixes.problem: Nepali news writes 'establishment faction' as संस्थापन पक्ष. स्थापित पक्ष is a calque of the English.
language_fixes.fix: संस्थापन पक्षले १५औं साधारण महाधिवेशन २ देखि ५ अक्टोबरसम्म तय गरेको काठमाडौं पोस्टले जनाएको छ।

nepali.editor: Two lines are stronger than the record: 'postpone' became रोक्न, and 'moving toward' Thapa's committee became समितिमा गइरहेको. The caption hook also misuses मनोनयन and repeats the card, and several sentences need craft fixes.

image_brief.alt_text: An illustration symbolising a political party divided into two separate paths under one banner, in muted red and blue tones.

angles.claim: The rival Deuba faction does not recognise the Thapa-led convention at all and is not expected to take part in the October 5 nominations; it has set its own ward-convention and general-convention timetable running into December (Mangsir), a split that none of the four stories on today's nomination date mention.
angles.why_it_matters: If the party's largest rival faction is organising a parallel process, the October 5 nomination date and the 'no panel, vote for individuals' rule apply only to one half of a divided party, not to Nepali Congress as a whole. Readers told simply that nominations open October 5 would not know the convention itself is contested.

evidence.fact: At a meeting at Deuba's residence, the faction decided not to participate in the convention being organised by the Thapa-led leadership and said it would proceed with its own convention schedule.
The Deuba camp has been preparing its own convention, with the central gathering planned for December.
A meeting at Deuba's residence in Chunadevi decided to complete ward conventions by October 15 and hold the general convention in Mangsir, while the establishment had set the convention in Ashoj.

angles.claim: The legal authority behind the Thapa leadership that is running this nomination process is still under Supreme Court review: the court recognised Thapa's committee in April 2026, but in August 2026 admitted a review petition from Deuba and Khadka challenging that very ruling, and the review has not been resolved.
angles.why_it_matters: Nominations are proceeding under a leadership whose legal standing a sitting Supreme Court bench has agreed to re-examine. If the review eventually goes against Thapa, decisions taken at this convention, including whoever is elected October 5 onward, could face a fresh legitimacy challenge.

evidence.fact: The Supreme Court in April recognised Thapa's leadership, and in August allowed Deuba and Khadka to seek a review of that ruling; the original decision has not been suspended.
Outgoing president Sher Bahadur Deuba's side filed a review petition at the Supreme Court against its earlier ruling that validated the Thapa-led committee elected at the special convention.
The Supreme Court cleared the legal obstacle for both Thapa's and Deuba's sides to proceed with convention preparations while the authority dispute and review request remain pending (विचाराधीन).

angles.claim: On the same day OnlineKhabar quoted Vice President Bishwa Prakash Sharma saying the convention will have 'no panel system,' DC Nepal reported a Congress leader, Dulal, describing panel formation at various levels of the party as a normal part of internal democratic practice, indicating the no-panel claim is not uncontested inside the party itself.
angles.why_it_matters: The 'no panels, vote for individuals' framing is being carried by multiple outlets as settled party policy on the strength of one vice president's statement. A same-day report describing panels as an ongoing, accepted practice at other levels suggests the picture is more mixed than the headline rule implies.

evidence.fact: The report quotes a Congress leader identified as Dulal describing competition through panel formation at various levels as a natural internal democratic practice within the party.
Vice President Bishwa Prakash Sharma told OnlineKhabar there would be no panel system and delegates would be free to vote for candidates of their choice.

angles.claim: Nepal Press reported that elections of convention representatives at the local level have already split unofficially along Thapa and Deuba lines, with factionalism increasing in the districts, even as the party sets 'no panel' rules for the central vote.
angles.why_it_matters: If delegate selection below the central level is already running along factional blocs, the 'delegates vote freely for individuals' framing for the October 5 central nominations describes the rule at the top while the underlying contest below it still runs on faction lines, a pattern worth checking before taking the no-panel claim at face value.

evidence.fact: "Elections have been fought in the name of Deuba and Thapa factions."

unanswered.question: Will the Deuba/Khadka faction register any central committee nominations on October 5, or boycott the process entirely, and if so what share of the roughly 7,500 delegates does each faction claim?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepali Congress Central Election Committee; Deuba-faction leaders Dr. Shekhar Koirala and Deepak Khadka

unanswered.question: What is the current status and expected timeline of the Supreme Court's review of its April ruling recognising Thapa's leadership, and could a later ruling unwind decisions made at this convention?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Supreme Court registrar's office; petitioners' counsel Maniram Upadhyay

unanswered.question: DC Nepal quotes a leader named Dulal describing panel formation as normal practice 'at various levels' - at which levels (district, province) are panels reportedly still being formed even as the centre bans them for the Central Working Committee vote?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Nepali Congress Central Election Committee chair; the leader identified as Dulal in DC Nepal's report; district-level NC office bearers

unanswered.question: If the Deuba faction proceeds with its own general convention in Mangsir as planned, which authority - the Election Commission or the courts - would determine which convention's elected leadership the state recognises as Nepali Congress going forward?
unanswered.who_could_answer: Election Commission of Nepal spokesperson; constitutional law experts

investigation.summary: Every outlet carrying today's story reports the October 5 nomination date and VP Bishwa Prakash Sharma's 'no panel' pledge as if Nepali Congress is proceeding as one party; none mention that the rival Deuba faction rejects the convention's legitimacy outright, has a Supreme Court review pending against the very ruling that recognises Thapa's leadership, and is organising its own parallel convention for Mangsir. Nepal Wire can also point to a same-day DC Nepal report in which another Congress leader described panel formation as still-normal practice, a detail at odds with the no-panel framing that other outlets reported uncritically.

ranking.reason: This is fresh and verified: DC Nepal and Ekantipur carry the October 5 nomination date, and VP Bishwa Prakash Sharma gave his no-panel statement on record to OnlineKhabar. It must be written as one leader's stated position, with OnlineKhabar's September 28 report of rival rule-sets showing the dispute is not settled. Weakest dimension: emotional charge.

Confirmed. DC Nepal and Ekantipur carry the October 5 nomination date, and VP Bishwa Prakash Sharma's no-panel rule is his on-record position to OnlineKhabar, set against OnlineKhabar's September 28 report of rival rule-sets. Weakest dimension: emotional charge.

findings.passage: What four reports left out: half the party is boycotting it and building its own convention for December instead.
findings.problem: The caption hook asserts a precise 50/50 split ('half the party') that no source in the record supports. The article's own 'What we still do not know' section admits the Central Election Committee has not published any delegate breakdown by faction, and Kathmandu Post reported more than 30 leaders moving from Deuba to Thapa, suggesting Deuba's side may be shrinking, not half. This is an invented number presented as fact in the most widely shared field.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the word 'half'. Write something like: 'What four reports left out: the Deuba camp is boycotting it entirely and building its own convention for December instead.'

findings.passage: None of today's reports on the October 5 nomination date mention that the rules they describe, no panels, delegates voting individually, apply only to the roughly 7,500 delegates attending the Thapa led gathering.
findings.problem: This states as settled fact that the 7,500 delegate figure excludes Deuba's camp entirely. But the article's own 'What we still do not know' section says Nepali Congress has not published a breakdown of how many of the roughly 7,500 delegates each faction claims as its own. The two sections directly contradict each other; the 'missed' section asserts a fact the record does not establish.
findings.suggested_fix: Soften to: 'It is not clear whether the roughly 7,500 delegates cited today include Deuba's camp at all, since Nepali Congress has not published a faction breakdown.' Keep this consistent with the unanswered-questions bullet.

findings.passage: Former Vice President Purna Bahadur Khadka led Deuba's faction for several months.
findings.problem: Search results (OnlineKhabar, Kathmandu Post, Desh Sanchar coverage of Khadka) consistently refer to him as Nepali Congress's former acting president, not former vice president. First mention of a named person must carry their correct role per house style; misstating a senior politician's title is a basic accuracy error.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'Purna Bahadur Khadka, Nepali Congress's former acting president, led Deuba's faction for several months.'

findings.passage: He too has now sided with Thapa's establishment, Kathmandu Post reported.
findings.problem: A September 18 OnlineKhabar report shows Khadka, as acting leader of the Deuba camp, publicly urging Gagan Thapa to postpone the convention and warning that two separate conventions could split the party, language inconsistent with having already 'sided with Thapa's establishment'. The cited Kathmandu Post article (September 16) was not independently verified here to carry this characterization, and it may overstate a more conditional or partial shift.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-check the Kathmandu Post article's exact wording on Khadka before publication. If it describes a partial or conditional move rather than full alignment, quote the specific language Kathmandu Post used rather than the newsroom's own paraphrase 'sided with'.

findings.passage: The Supreme Court ruled in Thapa's favour, but Deuba's camp has since asked the same court to review its own ruling.
findings.problem: The sole cited source for the original ruling is News on Air, an Indian government broadcaster rebroadcasting Nepali news, not a Nepali court record or primary Nepali outlet. House style requires preferring the original outlet for Nepal stories, and a foreign state broadcaster is a weak link for a domestic legal fact central to the story's legitimacy question. No date is given for this ruling either, violating the house rule that every claim carries a calendar date.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite a Nepali outlet's direct report of the ruling (e.g. Kathmandu Post's April coverage) and add the ruling's date, e.g. 'In April, the Supreme Court ruled in Thapa's favour.'

findings.passage:
CONGRESS SETS OCT 5
AS DEUBA CAMP BOYCOTTS
findings.problem: As of the October 3 run date, Deuba has urged a boycott but October 5 has not happened yet, so 'BOYCOTTS' states a future, contested action as an already-completed fact on the card, which circulates alone without context. This overstates certainty on a screenshot that readers will not see caveated.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'AS DEUBA CAMP TO BOYCOTT' or 'AS DEUBA URGES BOYCOTT' to match the not-yet-occurred status.

findings.passage: The headline: 'Nepali Congress sets October 5 nominations as Deuba faction boycotts.'
findings.problem: Search evidence (Radio Nepal) shows Deuba's rival camp is also calling its own December gathering the '15th general convention', meaning both factions are competing for the same official numbering and title, not just holding separate events. The piece's 'What the coverage missed' section, which exists specifically to flag what other outlets missed, itself omits this naming fight, weakening its own premise.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a line noting both factions claim the '15th General Convention' title, which sharpens the legitimacy dispute the piece is built around.

findings.passage: Four outlets reported today's nomination date, and all four missed that Nepali Congress now runs as two parties.
findings.problem: Nepali Congress remains a single registered party with a contested leadership dispute before the Supreme Court; no source establishes it legally 'runs as two parties'. The phrase is rhetorically stronger than the record, which describes rival factions and rival conventions, not two separate legal entities.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'all four missed that Nepali Congress is now run by two rival camps holding two separate conventions.'

findings.passage:
CONGRESS SETS OCT 5
AS DEUBA CAMP BOYCOTTS
findings.problem: House style calls for two lines of five to six words on the card headline; both lines here run only four words each, which can read as clipped or less punchy than the format intends.
findings.suggested_fix: Consider 'CONGRESS SETS OCT 5 VOTE' and 'AS DEUBA CAMP VOWS BOYCOTT' to fill out five to six words per line while staying under 24 characters.

red_team.summary: The piece has a genuinely strong premise, that four outlets covered half the Nepali Congress story, but it undercuts itself with an invented 'half the party' figure in the caption and an unsupported claim in its own 'What the coverage missed' section that directly contradicts its own 'What we still do not know' bullet. A politician's title is misstated and a foreign state broadcaster is used as the sole source for a core domestic legal fact, both fixable with better sourcing discipline. The underlying angle, two rival conventions and a pending Supreme Court review, is newsworthy and well suited to the reader test, but the piece needs tighter fact-checking before the strong hook can be trusted.

responses.response: The caption asserts a 50/50 split that no source supports, and it directly contradicts the article's own admission that the Central Election Committee has not published a faction breakdown and that Kathmandu Post reported Deuba losing more than 30 leaders. This is an invented precision in the field most people will actually read.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the caption hook to: 'Nepali Congress says voting opens October 5. What four reports left out: the Deuba camp is boycotting it entirely and building its own convention for December instead.'

responses.response: The red team is right that this line states as settled fact something the article itself later says is unknown. The two sections cannot both be true. The piece should not assert the 7,500 figure excludes Deuba's camp when the closing section says that breakdown has not been published.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'None of today's reports say whether the roughly 7,500 delegate figure includes Deuba's camp at all. Nepali Congress has not published a breakdown by faction.'

responses.response: Checked against Kathmandu Post's own October 2025 reporting: Deuba handed the acting presidency to Khadka, described there as the party's vice president at the time, who then served as acting president while leading the Deuba camp. The role that matters for this sentence, the one under which he 'led Deuba's faction for several months,' is acting president, not vice president. The current text understates and misdates his role.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'Purna Bahadur Khadka, Nepali Congress's former acting president, led Deuba's faction for several months.'

responses.response: We cannot confirm from the record in hand that Kathmandu Post's September 16 report used language as strong as 'sided with Thapa's establishment,' and a close-in-time OnlineKhabar report shows Khadka still acting as a Deuba camp figure pushing for postponement. Until the exact Kathmandu Post wording is reverified, the paraphrase risks overstating a shift that may be partial or conditional.
responses.proposed_edit: Re-check the Kathmandu Post September 16 article's exact phrasing before publication. If it stops short of full alignment, write: 'He has since moved toward Thapa's committee, Kathmandu Post reported,' and attribute any stronger characterization directly to the paper's own words.

responses.response: House style prefers Nepali outlets over aggregators and foreign broadcasters for Nepal stories, and every claim should carry a date. News on Air is an Indian state broadcaster rebroadcasting Nepali news, and this sentence has no date for a ruling central to the whole legitimacy question of the story. Both problems are fixable with a cited Nepali outlet.
responses.proposed_edit: Cite Kathmandu Post's own report of the ruling with its date, e.g. 'In April, the Supreme Court ruled in Thapa's favour, Kathmandu Post reported,' and keep News on Air only as secondary corroboration if needed.

responses.response: As of the October 3 run date, the boycott is a call Deuba has made, not a completed action, since October 5 has not happened yet. A card headline that circulates alone should not state a future, contested event as a finished fact.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the second line to 'AS DEUBA CAMP VOWS BOYCOTT' so the card matches the not-yet-occurred status.

responses.response: If both camps are indeed claiming the same '15th General Convention' title, that is a concrete, checkable detail that sharpens the legitimacy fight the piece is built on, and a 'what the coverage missed' section should not itself miss it. We should verify the Radio Nepal detail directly before adding it, but if confirmed it belongs in the piece.
responses.proposed_edit: After verifying with Radio Nepal or another outlet, add to the 'What the coverage missed' section: 'Both camps are calling their gathering the party's 15th General Convention, Radio Nepal reported, each claiming the same title as the other.'

responses.response: Nepali Congress remains one registered party with a leadership dispute before the courts. 'Runs as two parties' overstates the legal reality the record supports, which is rival factions and rival conventions, not two legal entities. The body text gets this right with 'holding two' conventions; the take line should match that precision.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: 'Four outlets reported today's nomination date, and all four missed that Nepali Congress is now run by two rival camps holding two separate conventions.'

responses.response: House style calls for five to six words per line on the card headline, and both lines here run four words. This is a minor format miss, but it is a clear, written rule, so it should be fixed.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to 'CONGRESS SETS OCT 5 VOTE' and 'AS DEUBA CAMP VOWS BOYCOTT', both within the 24 character limit and closer to the five to six word target.

defense.summary: The red team's findings are largely sound and the defence accepts all nine. The most serious issues are two internal contradictions: the caption's invented 'half the party' split and the body's claim that the 7,500 delegate count excludes Deuba's camp both directly contradict the article's own closing admission that no faction breakdown has been published. Khadka's role is misstated as vice president when the record shows he led Deuba's faction as acting president, and the characterization of his shift to Thapa needs re-verification against the exact Kathmandu Post wording. The Supreme Court ruling needs a Nepali source and a date rather than a dateless citation to an Indian state broadcaster. The card headline overstates a not-yet-occurred boycott as settled fact and falls short of the house style word count. The 'two parties' line in the take overstates the legal reality the body itself gets right. All fixes are small, surgical edits rather than rewrites.

rulings.note: No source supports 'half the party'. Kathmandu Post reports Deuba's side losing more than 30 leaders, and the article admits no faction breakdown exists. The invented split sits in the most read field.
This contradicts the article's own 'What we still do not know' bullet. Setopati gives about 7,500 delegates with no faction split, so the sentence must not say the figure covers only Thapa's side.
Khadka led the Deuba camp as acting president. 'Former Vice President' leaves out the role that matters for this sentence. Medium.
The September 18 OnlineKhabar report has Khadka still urging postponement as Deuba camp leader. 'Sided with' must be cut back to wording the cited Kathmandu Post piece carries.
The ruling is a core legal fact. It rests on an Indian state broadcaster and carries no date. Do not insert 'April' unless a Nepali source in the list states it.

The record says Deuba urged a boycott. The card states it as a completed act. Line 1 is also unreadable alone, since it never says what is set for October 5. The defence's replacement fails too. 'AS DEUBA CAMP VOWS BOYCOTT' is 26 characters, and 'VOWS' is stronger than 'urges'.
Not required for publication. The editor may add the naming dispute only if the Radio Nepal report is confirmed and added to the sources list with attribution.
Nepali Congress is one party with rival camps. 'Runs as two parties' is stronger than the record.

Both card lines run four words, short of the style rule. The defence fix 'CONGRESS SETS OCT 5 VOTE' is also wrong, because October 5 is nomination registration, not a vote. The replacement card is given in the edits.

judge_1.reason: The two convention angle is real and well sourced, but the piece invents a 'half the party' split and states a delegate breakdown its own closing section says does not exist.
